transcript.text: I can help with that. The most common reason a washing machine won't spin is that it hasn't drained the water first; the machine has a safety feature that prevents spinning if there is still water in the drum. This is often caused by a blockage in the pump filter or drain hose. Could you please check the pump filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) to see if it is blocked? Also, when you start a cycle, does the machine attempt to drain the water before stopping?
it drains fine, no water left in the drum. just came out dripping wet after the wash, it tries to spin then gives up. do i really need to do the filter?

You don't need to do the filter yet if it drains well. Since it drains but won't spin, the most common cause is an unbalanced load (like one heavy item) or a programme that doesn't use high speed (like 'delicate'). Did you have a single heavy item in there, or was it set to a gentle cycle?
yeah it was just the big heavy rubber backed bath mat on its own, the dogs muddy it. normal 1000 setting not delicate

That explains it perfectly. A single heavy rubber-backed bath mat is a classic cause for this: the water makes it stick to one side of the drum, and the machine detects an imbalance so it refuses to spin at high speed to avoid banging itself apart. This is normal safety behaviour, not a fault. To fix it next time, either wash the mat with some towels or other items to balance the load, or run a 'Drain & Spin' cycle immediately after the wash (with the mat inside) to extract as much water as possible before you take it out. If you try spinning just that mat on its own again and it still refuses to spin even when damp/heavy, let me know.
